page: Microsoft Azure D4a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache hierarchy consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI are enabled, alongside AVX, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 extensions and AMX units are absent. The instance does not include a GPU and comes equipped with 107 GB of local SSD temporary storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance alongside lower multi-core and throughput metrics due to its compact 4-vCPU layout. In synthetic tests, the instance registered a strong single-core stress-ng score of 2,704.79 (top 25%), while multi-core stress-ng registered at 5,400.98 (bottom 25%). Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 1,571.0 and a multi-core score of 3,618.0, with average performance in text processing (1,911.0) and gzip compression (26.22 GB/sec single-threaded). Workloads demanding heavy parallelism—such as clang software compilation (3,843.0), ray tracing (4,630.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (21.39 GB/sec)—placed within the lower quartile of tested environments.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average performance under uncached read conditions at 40.46 GB/sec for 256MB blocks, paired with a lower uncached write throughput of 24.31 GB/sec. Application testing reflected 3.95 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, 5.05 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and 1,849.52 on PassMark database operations, placing these data services in the bottom 25% of fleet comparisons. For lightweight machine learning workloads, small model (135M) text generation executed at 113.01 tokens/sec (middle 50%), though prompt processing throughput was constrained at 313.19 tokens/sec.

Given its balanced CPU-to-memory ratio and dedicated AMD EPYC compute cores, Microsoft Azure D4a_v4 offers an efficient cost profile for low- to moderate-concurrency general-purpose applications. While unsuited for dense multi-threaded compilation, intensive vector calculations, or heavy database deployments, the instance is well suited for web serving, microservices, development environments, and lightweight API backends.
description: Microsoft Azure D4a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), and 107 GB of local SSD storage, without GPU acceleration. It includes standard instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, but lacks AVX-512 extensions. In benchmark evaluations, the D4a_v4 achieves strong single-core CPU throughput (stress-ng score of 2,704.79) alongside average single-threaded compression and text processing performance. However, multi-core scaling, memory write bandwidth (24.31 GB/sec), and database operations place in the lower quartile of comparative benchmarks. This instance delivers an efficient hardware allocation for moderate-scale web serving, microservices, lightweight API gateways, and general enterprise application hosting.
